analysis_notes.source_text_analysis: The source text (torah_104.txt) consists of 3 lines. Line 1: Rebbe Nachman loved simple people's worship and those who could say many supplications (תְּחִנּוֹת וּבַקָּשׁוֹת) from the large siddurim, in the manner of the simple common folk. Line 2: He would warn and rebuke those who considered themselves wise but did not exert themselves to sing Shabbat songs (זְמִירוֹת בְּשַׁבָּת), saying that the essence of Judaism is simplicity and complete sincerity (פְּשִׁיטוּת וּבִתְמִימוּת גָּמוּר), without any sophistications. Line 3: He himself, before the heavy illness from which he passed away, would sing many Shabbat songs every Shabbat and Motza'ei Shabbat. No bechina language appears anywhere in this text. The concepts mentioned — זְמִירוֹת (Shabbat songs), תְּחִנּוֹת וּבַקָּשׁוֹת (supplications), פְּשִׁיטוּת (simplicity), תְּמִימוּת (sincerity/wholeness) — are not equated with each other via bechina formulations. They are practical behavioral descriptions, not conceptual identifications.

analysis_notes.torah_character_note: LM2 Torah 104 belongs to the category of biographical/practical notes in Likutay Moharan Tinyana — entries that report Rebbe Nachman's personal conduct and ethical guidance without formal kabbalistic-conceptual structure. Torah 104 is similar in character to Torah 103 but even simpler — it is purely descriptive.
